items: **Availability:** if a node dies, another has the data.
**Latency:** put replicas near users in other regions.

blocks.text: The fundamental tension: the moment you have more than one copy, you must decide what happens when copies disagree — and how long a write waits for other copies before it's acknowledged.

blocks.caption: Writes go to the leader; followers apply its log

blocks.text: The leader appends every change to its write-ahead log (or binlog) and streams it to followers, which apply it in the same order. This is how Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB replica sets and most managed databases work.

head: Mode
Write latency
Data loss on leader failure
rows: Last few writes may be lost
None if the sync follower survives
Slowest; one slow follower blocks writes

sections.title: Replication lag and the anomalies it causes

head: Anomaly
Example
Fix
rows: User edits profile, reloads, sees the old value from a lagging replica
Read own data from the leader for a few seconds after writing, or track the write's LSN
Refreshing alternates between replicas — data appears then disappears
Pin a user's reads to one replica
A reply appears before the question it answers
Keep causally related writes in one partition / order

blocks.title: Key insight
blocks.text: Lag is usually milliseconds, but under load or after a failover it can be seconds or minutes. Design for the worst case on any path where staleness matters.

items.title: Elect
items.text: Choose the most up-to-date follower (via consensus or an orchestrator).

items.title: Reconfigure
items.text: Point clients/proxies at the new leader.

items.title: Fence
items.text: Make sure the old leader can't accept writes if it comes back (split brain).

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text: Automatic failover with async replication can silently lose the last acknowledged writes — and if those writes generated IDs used elsewhere (e.g. in a cache), you get inconsistencies. Say which you prefer: brief unavailability or possible loss.

cols.title: Multi-leader
pros: Writes in every region with local latency
cons: Write conflicts — needs LWW, CRDTs or custom merge

cols.title: Leaderless (Dynamo-style)
pros: Any replica accepts writes; quorum reads/writes
cons: Eventual consistency; read repair and anti-entropy needed

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: I'd use single-leader replication with one synchronous follower for durability, asynchronous read replicas for scale, and route a user's reads to the leader right after they write.
